idea: Home-style tiffin delivery for hostel students in Bidholi, Dehradun

strategist.problem: Hostel students in Bidholi face a 45-minute walk or ₹30-50 auto ride to reach the nearest decent restaurant, and by 8:00 PM on weekdays, they are either eating stale canteen food or skipping dinner due to fatigue and lack of affordable, home-cooked options within walking distance of their hostels.
strategist.target_customer: UG and PG students residing in hostels within a 1.5 km radius of UPES Bidholi campus, aged 18-24, who spend ₹1,500-₹2,500 monthly on food and actively seek reliable, hot, home-style meals delivered to their hostel gates by 7:30 PM to avoid the hassle of finding external food vendors.
strategist.mission: Deliver fresh, home-style tiffins directly to hostel gates in Bidholi by 7:30 PM daily, ensuring students get a nutritious, affordable meal without leaving their accommodation.

competitors.name: UPES Canteen and Mess Services
competitors.differentiator: We offer varied, home-style recipes and on-demand flexibility, whereas the canteen serves repetitive, institutional food with fixed, often crowded, dining hours.

competitors.name: Swiggy and Zomato Delivery Partners
competitors.differentiator: We eliminate ₹40-60 delivery fees and high platform commissions, offering a flat, predictable monthly subscription price for daily meals, which is significantly cheaper than ordering single items via apps.

competitors.name: Local Bidholi Street Food Vendors
competitors.differentiator: We provide hygienic, packaged, and consistent home-cooked meals, whereas street vendors lack hygiene guarantees, consistent quality, and the convenience of direct hostel gate delivery.

scope_cuts: Building a custom mobile app or website for ordering; we will use WhatsApp Business and Google Forms for initial subscriptions and menu selection to save development time and costs.

Offering breakfast or lunch services; we focus exclusively on dinner (7:00-8:00 PM) to streamline kitchen operations, reduce food waste, and match the peak hunger time for students returning from classes.
Expanding beyond the 1.5 km radius of UPES Bidholi; we restrict delivery to hostels within walking distance or short auto rides to maintain low logistics costs and ensure food arrives hot.

stack.name: WhatsApp Business
stack.why: Zero-cost, high-open-rate channel for daily menu updates and direct hostel gate delivery coordination.

stack.name: Google Forms
stack.why: Free, structured tool for collecting weekly meal preferences and subscription sign-ups without building a custom app.

stack.name: Razorpay Payment Links
stack.why: Instant, no-code UPI integration for collecting monthly ₹1,500-₹2,500 subscriptions directly in WhatsApp chats.

stack.name: Canva Free
stack.why: Creates daily digital menu cards and WhatsApp status graphics without hiring a designer.

ai_tools.name: Claude Code
ai_tools.why: Generates the exact WhatsApp Business auto-reply scripts and Google Form logic for the subscription flow.

ai_tools.name: v0
ai_tools.why: Renders a simple, mobile-friendly HTML landing page for the subscription pitch if a link is needed outside WhatsApp.

mvp_features: SKU 1: 30-Day Dinner Subscription (₹1,800/month) - 30x 350g home-style tiffins (1 sabzi, 2 rotis, 1 dal, 1 salad, 1 sweet), delivered to hostel gates by 7:30 PM daily.
SKU 2: 10-Day Trial Pack (₹650) - 10x 350g tiffins for students hesitant to commit to a full month, valid for 2 consecutive weeks.
SKU 3: Weekly Custom Menu Selection - Students use Google Forms every Sunday to choose from 3 rotating home-style recipes for the upcoming week.
first_10_steps: Secure a compliant cooking space (e.g., a friend's PG with a kitchen or a local home-kitchen rental) and verify hostel rules regarding external food delivery to gates.
Set up a WhatsApp Business account on a dedicated phone number and configure the 'Quick Reply' feature with 5 pre-set messages for menu, pricing, and delivery times.
Create a Google Form titled 'UPES Bidholi Tiffin Subscription' with 4 fields: Name, Hostel Name, Meal Preference (Veg/Non-Veg), and Payment Status.
Design 3 digital menu cards using Canva Free, featuring high-resolution photos of the 3 rotating home-style recipes, and save them as 1080x1080 PNG files.
Visit 3 local vegetable and spice vendors in Dehradun's Sadar Bazaar to negotiate bulk weekly rates for 50kg of rice, 20kg of dal, and 10kg of paneer, securing a 10% discount for cash payments.
Purchase 500 units of 400ml eco-friendly disposable tiffin containers and 500 units of 200ml sauce cups from a local Dehradun packaging supplier for a total of ₹4,500.
Generate a Razorpay Payment Link for the ₹1,800 monthly subscription and the ₹650 10-day trial pack, testing the UPI flow with a ₹1 self-payment.
Post the Canva menu cards and the Google Form link in 5 active UPES hostel WhatsApp groups, offering a free 1-day trial tiffin to the first 10 respondents.

Cook and pack 15 sample tiffins (350g each) in the secured kitchen space on a Tuesday evening, delivering them personally to 3 different hostels within the 1.5 km radius by 7:30 PM to test logistics and food temperature.

Collect feedback from the 15 sample recipients via a 3-question WhatsApp voice note, adjusting the spice level and roti thickness based on their specific requests, and finalize the supplier order for the first 30-day batch of ingredients (approx. ₹8,000).

pricing.name: 30-Day Dinner Subscription
features: 30x 350g home-style tiffins (1 sabzi, 2 rotis, 1 dal, 1 salad, 1 sweet)
Daily delivery to hostel gates by 7:30 PM
Weekly custom menu selection via Google Forms

revenue_targets.notes: Initial cohort from 3 hostels via WhatsApp groups and free trial tiffins
Expansion to 5 hostels, word-of-mouth and referral incentives
Stabilized base with 80% retention, added 2 new hostels

key_assumptions: Students are willing to pay ₹1,800/month for home-style tiffins, which is 20% cheaper than ordering 30 single meals via Swiggy/Zomato (approx ₹2,250 + delivery fees).
Food cost per tiffin is ₹40 (₹1,200/month), based on bulk purchasing from Sadar Bazaar vendors at negotiated rates.
Marketing spend of ₹1,500/month covers printed flyers, free trial tiffins for acquisition, and occasional WhatsApp broadcast boosts.
Delivery is handled by the founder and one part-time batchmate, costing ₹0 in direct cash outflow but consuming 2 hours daily.

channels.name: Hostel WhatsApp Group Seeding
channels.tactic: Post a 150-word offer with a free tiffin voucher in 5 active UPES Bidholi hostel WhatsApp groups (2 posts/week), targeting 50 unique students/week

channels.name: Student Ambassador Room-to-Room Sampling
channels.tactic: Recruit 1 student ambassador per target hostel (3 total) to distribute 10 free 100g tiffin samples to roommates between 6:00-6:30 PM daily, bypassing gate security restrictions

first_10_customers: Day 1-2: Identify 3 hostels within 1.5km of UPES Bidholi (e.g., UPES Boys Hostel, nearby private PGs) and find the WhatsApp group admins or wardens via Instagram DMs or direct visits.
Day 3-4: Cook 10 free 350g tiffins and deliver them personally to 10 specific students in those hostels, asking for a 2-minute feedback call and a photo of the meal.
Day 5-7: Use the 10 photos and feedback to create a 15-second Instagram Reel and a WhatsApp status, tagging the hostels and asking for referrals.
Day 8-10: DM 20 students who engaged with the Reel or status, offering a ₹200 discount on the first 10-day trial pack if they subscribe within 48 hours.
Day 11-14: Follow up with the 10 initial free-tiffin recipients, converting them to paying 30-day subscribers by highlighting the consistency and the 7:30 PM gate delivery guarantee.
Day 15-21: Ask each of the first 5 paying customers to forward the offer to 2 friends in their hostel, offering a ₹100 credit for each new subscriber who completes a 10-day trial.
growth.cold_message: Hi [Name], I'm a UPES student delivering home-style tiffins to hostel gates by 7:30 PM. I'm offering a free 350g dinner tiffin today to 5 students in [Hostel Name]—want me to drop one at your gate? No cost, just want to ensure it's hot and tasty before you decide on a monthly plan.

objections.objection: I can just order from Swiggy or Zomato, why should I pay ₹1,800/month for a tiffin?
objections.response: Swiggy/Zomato charges ₹40-60 delivery fees per order, so 30 dinners cost you over ₹2,500 plus platform commissions. Our ₹1,800/month is a flat rate with zero delivery fees, and you get a consistent, home-cooked meal without the app hassle.

objections.objection: I'm not sure I'll stick to a 30-day commitment, what if I don't like the food?
objections.response: Start with our 10-Day Trial Pack for ₹650. If you don't like it, you don't pay for the 30-day plan. We also offer a 'first tiffin free' guarantee for new subscribers—if your first delivery isn't hot and fresh, your next 3 days are on us.

critic.verdict: The plan is highly realistic and tightly constrained to the founder's student status and budget, avoiding common startup pitfalls like app development. The focus on a single SKU (dinner) and local logistics makes it executable within the 15-hour weekly limit. The primary weakness is the financial model, which underestimates the operational costs of a physical food business, leading to an optimistic runway calculation.
critic.biggest_risk: The plan assumes a monthly burn of only ₹3,500, which excludes the variable cost of goods (ingredients) and likely underestimates fixed costs like kitchen access; if actual burn is closer to ₹8,000-₹10,000, the ₹15,000 capital provides less than 2 months of runway before the first significant revenue, creating a cash-flow crisis if customer acquisition is slower than projected.
